density_challenge: The opposite case: the overview is not a standalone 8-minute film, because the list itself rests on very little. The only first-hand statement of what was sent is one sentence in Qureshi (line 46) with his own hedge. Everything else is a single clause: Mabrey (Impro, past tense), Agrawal (Looming Tower, 'mandatory'), Saraf (GTD, 'eventually mandated'), plus a 2016 journalist, one HN comment saying 'two books', and one anonymous HN reply saying 'optional'. No Palantir source names any book, and for Interviewing Users and Principles there is no stated reason at all. Most of the explorer's 'mechanisms' (FDE-PD loop, Airbus, data-access politics, S-1 platform language) are about the FDE model in general and would be true if the reading list never existed. They fill the film but do not explain the list, so a viewer could come away with a Palantir-FDE explainer and the books as a pretext; those topics likely belong to the per-book units or a separate FDE video. The links between a book and a mechanism are mostly authors' or explorer's glosses: Looming Tower to 'shared enemy' is the explorer's reading of Agrawal, Interviewing Users to FDE trust is inference only, and 'Impro 三种读法' pairs three sources that answer different questions (outward reading rooms, inward status, a critic's jab). Independence is thin: Saraf cites Qureshi, and Mabrey's remark may come from the Karp-Zamiska book. On that view the honest unit is a 3-4 minute 'what we can and cannot say' short, with the longer FDE material parked elsewhere. The case for standalone still holds on one point: the evidence-grading itself (wording from 'sent a copy' to 'mandatory' to 'optional', reposts inflating to five books on day one, official pages silent) is a self-contained and checkable story, and that part is accurate as verified. My recommendation is standalone only if the film is about the claim and its evidence, not about FDE mechanics. Sources the explorer missed or left unopened: Karp and Zamiska, The Technological Republic, chapter 'The Improvisational Startup' (the primary text for the Mabrey/Robbins/New Republic claim); Sarah Constantin's 'The Great Data Integration Schlep' (cited by Qureshi footnote [3], bears on the data-politics mechanism); Byrne Hobart's piece on the company (footnote [5]); The Generalist's 'Palantir's Weirdest Book Recommendation' (paywalled, secondary); Barry McCardel's post (barry.ooo/posts/fde-culture, ex-Palantir; I checked and it has no book mentions, so low value). Sean Goedecke's post and Thorsten Ball's newsletter repeat Qureshi and are not independent.
